# Party Access Functions

A reusable Compute Definition providing helpers for party names, participant channels, reader access, agreed terms and activation guards. These functions return values or raise failures; they do not activate a document, change permissions or emit events. Document paths refer to the document in which the functions execute.

## Parties and readers

- `validPartyName(candidate)` accepts nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. It imposes no further naming restriction.
- `transports(roster)` builds a channel map from each party’s `lead/channel` and each representative’s `channel`. Party entries use the role name; representatives use `role__repId`. Missing channels default to `{}` and missing `representatives` to `{}`.
- `readerGroups(readers, roster)` starts with the supplied named reader groups, then adds each party’s and representative’s `readerKeys` under the same names. Generated entries overwrite matching names in `readers`. Missing `readerKeys` default to `[]`.
- `authority(channel, state)` returns whether the text `channel` equals a role in `state.parties` or a `role__repId` for a representative currently listed there. Missing `parties` or `representatives` default to `{}`. This is a roster-name check, not authentication of an actor.

## Access validation

`accessValid(accessPaths, readers, roster)` checks the transports and reader groups built from its arguments. Their declared initial values are `[]`, `{}` and `{}`, respectively.

Every External Channel is exempt from this function’s access matching. Every other transport must be a Timeline Channel; otherwise it raises `ACTIVATION_CHANNEL_REQUIRED`.

For each Timeline Channel, at least one document resolved from `accessPaths` must satisfy all three conditions:

- Its `allowedTimelines` contains the channel’s exact `timeline` identity.
- Its `allowedKeys` contains at least one key from **every** reader group.
- Its provider at `/contracts/provider/provider` has the same exact identity as the channel’s `timeline/provider`.

All groups must be covered within one matching access document for that transport; grants from separate documents are not combined. Different transports may match different documents. An empty reader group cannot be satisfied; no reader groups means the key condition passes without a key match.

Every examined access path must resolve to a Timeline Access document, or the function raises `TIMELINE_ACCESS_DOCUMENT_REQUIRED`, even if another path already matched. Missing `allowedTimelines` and `allowedKeys` are read as `[]`; missing provider values are read as `{}` for comparison. A transport without a matching document makes the result false. With no transports, the result is true.

## Terms and activation

`termsCurrent()` compares each agreed value in `/activation/terms/fields` with the current document value at its corresponding path. Any difference returns false. A missing fields map defaults to `{}`, so no recorded comparisons returns true.

`businessReady()` returns true immediately when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires:

- `closed` to be false, using false when missing;
- an affirmative `approved/<role>` for every role in `required`, with missing approvals treated as false and missing `required` as `[]`;
- `termsCurrent()` to pass;
- `accessValid()` to pass using activation’s `accessPaths`, `readers` and `parties`, defaulting to `[]`, `{}` and `{}`.

It does not test `active` or set activation state. Access validation can raise its structural failures instead of returning false.

`requireActive(channel, workflow)` also returns true when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it checks, in order: `active` (missing means false), raising `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE`; access validity, raising `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING` for a false result; and, only when the Boolean `workflow` is true, roster authority for `channel`, raising `REPRESENTATIVE_NO_LONGER_AUTHORIZED` if absent. Access validation’s structural failures also propagate. This guard does not independently check `closed`, approvals or agreed terms.

These helpers do not verify provider publication, signatures or history completeness. A passing access check relies on established Timeline Access state; it does not itself confirm an external permission grant or successful business operation.
